answer: A newcomer earns standing by working one tide cycle at a boatyard, restoring ferrous fittings under a willow-sheltered workshop: each repair is photographed, signed by the boat owner, and entered in a public log, and two independent surveyors recheck a sample against the owner within five days. A duplicated entry or a second identity claiming the same fittings cancels the cycle, revokes the newcomer, and bars its sponsor for a season, so a thousand fakes would need a thousand cycles of real boatyard work, while one honest newcomer pays only one.
